public_rationale: The forecast has no deadline for the benefit or Nobel award. The 2026 Parisi–Zamponi paper documents useful AI assistance, but Parisi won in 2021, so it does not establish the future-laureate component. No qualifying decisive event was found by October 28, 2026.
limitations: The conclusion depends on reading future laureates as future recipients, rather than existing laureates doing later work.
Publication or use in 2026 does not by itself establish that an AI system was built in 2026.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: AI built in 2026 or 2027 will be valuable to future Nobel laureates.

statement.excerpt: I don’t doubt that AI built in 2026 or 2027 will be valuable to future Nobel Laureates.
statement.document_title: Nobel Prizes and The AI Hype Hall of Fame

our_interpretation: The years specify when the AI is built, not a deadline for its benefit or the Nobel award.
Valuable means materially assisting scientific work, rather than incidental use.
Future laureates means people who receive a Nobel Prize after the post. The assistance need not itself earn the prize.
The model-vintage restriction defines the eligible systems; it is not an if-then antecedent.
criteria.support_condition: A documented AI system built in 2026 or 2027 materially assists scientific work by someone subsequently confirmed as a Nobel laureate after the post.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Evidence would need to rule out qualifying benefit for all future laureates from the specified model cohort. Mere non-occurrence by a finite evaluation date cannot do that.
